findings.summary: A createMany failure on a dangling foreign key that slipped past a .filter() guard surfaces one generic constraint error for the whole batch, without naming which row was the offender, whereas the old per-row loop failed on the specific offending item.
findings.disposition: accepted, not fixed -- both forms roll back the same transaction to the same end state; the debuggability cost is real but marginal, and every .filter() guard is already an exact behavioral match to the loop's own continue it replaced, making a dangling reference reaching createMany a pre-existing data condition, not something this change makes more likely

findings.summary: A single createMany statement is capped by Postgres at 65,535 bind parameters; a same-depth bucket of roughly 1,800+ issues in one tenant's seed (Issue has 35+ scalar columns) would approach that ceiling and throw, a failure mode the old per-row loop never had.
findings.disposition: accepted, not fixed -- unexercised headroom rather than an active defect at this codebase's stated scale (hundreds of rows per tenant); tracked as a forward-looking limit rather than a blocking finding
